title: Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch
main_claim: For n>=3, if two smooth metrics on a compact connected manifold with boundary have the same local energy DN map with input and observation on one nonempty proper open boundary patch Γ, then g2 = Φ^*g1 for a smooth diffeomorphism Φ that fixes Γ. Corollaries: full-boundary uniqueness, and smooth scalar conductivity uniqueness from one patch.

issues.description: The paper asserts, but only sketches, that the moving-sphere Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator has the expansion B + rB_1 + r^2B_2 with smooth parameter dependence in the full classical symbol topology, with derivative allowances C_j β^j. Everything downstream (U ∈ εβ^{-|α|}Ψ^{2-|α|}, the bounds on J) depends on this. I believe it is standard parametrix-with-parameters material, but the paper does not write it out.
issues.evidence: The proof cites Joshi–Lionheart and argues via the decaying normal root and uniform invertibility of the rescaled Dirichlet problem for 0<=r<=r0. No explicit symbol estimates are given.

issues.description: The claim that the error operator E has count at most (3,1), splitting into exactly the three types εβ^{-1}Ψ^1∂^2, εΨ^2∂ and εβΨ^3, is argued by a bookkeeping rule plus a verbal argument that third base derivatives cancel. I checked the dangerous terms ([A∂, rQ∂∂], [fA^*B, rQ∂∂], [A∂, U_1∂], UZ) and they fit the types. The full expansion is not written out, though, and this is the spot where a hidden failure in the core estimate would most likely be.
issues.evidence: Spot checks: the third-order coefficient of [T^†,U] is the commutator of A with the real scalar rQ, which is 0. rQ·∂f ~ rβ^2 ≤ ε gives the εΨ^2∂ type. rQ·∂^2f ~ rβ^3 ≤ εβ gives the εβΨ^2 type.

coverage:
Read all eight sections in full. Checked by hand, and numerically where noted:
- Boundary jets: recovering h from (det h)h^{-1} when m>=2, and the highest-jet term trA - A(v,v) giving A=0.
- Variational competitor argument for the common cap and Green-kernel equality.
- Point-distribution duality for second jets and point separation.
- Cross-series lemma: singular-value decay, convergence from γ1+γ2>1, and the agreement argument.
- Product extension criterion: dual-cone splitting (covariance argument, rank-one extreme points from r(r+1)/2>2), the quadratic gap, cross placement, and the Carleman interpolation exponent, which is 1/2+κl/2 at e=0.
- Fixed-separation initialization: the three-ball exponent tends to 1, and the tube test.
- Section 4: conformal Hessian of the depth function, profile bounds (rβ^2 ≤ CR_*p^2ℓ^{p-2}), the strict moving-sphere test, Hess(r^2/2) = 2dr⊗dr + r^2 Hess f, ω·(U1-U2) = b·U2. A numerical minimization over v,w in n=3 shows the |b|^2 terms cancel, with minimum exactly 0 in the Euclidean case.
- Section 5: the P=2T+U+J decomposition, including D^+ commuting with r^{-1}A^* and the size of each coefficient; the Fischer-norm raising identity (N_{k+1}/N_k = 2d+2, harmonic projection norm); all three integrations by parts; the convex bound; the degree coefficient d-k-ϑ(n-1)+ϑζ(k+n-1); signs of the Hessian contribution (d-1+ϑ>0); the norm-comparison identity for E term by term; P1 bounded.
- Section 6: the moment bound, the metric system h∂∂v1 = -Q∂∂V, interpolation exponents (ηD = 1/2, m ≥ 10+3D), and the open/closed continuity argument.
- Section 7: maximal match, frontier partner, touching ball, surjectivity, boundary completion, and the fact that Φ fixes Γ.
- Section 8: energy and density conversion, and the Liouville boundary-rigidity ODE.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank198 (Determination of a metric and a unitary connection from one boundary patch, Oct 5 2026) reported no_gap_found and said it relies on this paper's angular coercivity count (3,1). My pass agrees: I spot-checked that count and found it consistent, but did not fully re-derive it. Nothing here depends on a companion paper, so there is no circularity.
